To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the practices of benefits-led approaches contribute to IT-enabled innovations, but that the practices have to applied in different ways to the context.
IT-enabled innovation requires a new approach to benefits realization, that involves the development of a new practice of ‘ideation’.
the practices of benefits-led approaches to IS can be applied to innovation, but they have to be adapted and applied in different ways to the context.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the implications of a paradigm shift in the way that organizations approach IT and its role in supporting innovation and change.
exploring IT-enabled innovation, which is a new and emerging phenomenon that is different from previous paradigns.
understanding how IT can contribute to innovation and the role of the IT function in innovation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no simple answers to the question posed in our title.
the practices of IT implementation, benefits management and innovation can be integrated to form a third paradigm, IT-enabled innovation.
there is no single best practice for IT-enabled innovation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IT can be used to facilitate the development and implementation of innovations.
the benefits realization paradigm is a good starting point, but the practices need to be modified to take account of the context and to include the practices of ideation.
innovation is a process that is enabled by a range of practices, some of which are similar to those used in a benefits-led approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the focus on benefits realization can be extended to include a broader range of outcomes, such as innovation, and that a planned approach to realizing benefits can be applied to innovation.
the practices that have emerged in the literature on benefits-led approaches are not sufficient to support innovation and new ways of working are needed to support the innovation agenda.
organizations need to develop a new practice of innovation and ideation to exploit new technology-enabled opportunities.
